gap: Glyph edges are soft: in the word "Down," A's edge pixels run 0.62 per core pixel across 205 distinct grey levels vs B's 0.55 across 23 — A's stems carry a visible halo where B's are cut clean, and it shows on the light ground at body size.
gapTheirs: No dimmed tier at all: B paints the `*` markers at full body ink (#1c1c1c on paper, #cccccc on the dark ground — identical to the prose, 0 px of grey in the marker box), while A drops them to #7a7a7a / #808080; and B's dark mode leaks a ghost heading at #1c1c1c on #1a1a1a — 1.01:1, neither hidden nor readable — that its light mode does not show.
verdict: Both grounds are the same paper and the same ink (#f9f9f9/#1c1c1c, #1a1a1a/#cccccc), so this comes down entirely to the third tier — the grey between prose and background — and only A has one. In B the asterisks around *never* are exactly as black as the sentence they wrap, so every emphasis you type punches two extra full-weight glyphs into the line; A pushes them back to a mid grey (4.0:1 on paper, 4.6:1 on the dark ground) and the prose stays the loudest thing on the page. Worse, B's dark side draws a heading at #1c1c1c on #1a1a1a — a smudge you can see on an OLED at night and cannot read anywhere, and which light mode does not produce: that is a palette arrived at by inverting values, not by choosing them. A's own dark side is not designed either — the dim grey sits at the same 57% alpha in both themes and the caret is the same raw #00b5ff on white as on black, which on paper is the brightest object in the frame — but a slightly soft stem is a smaller tax than markdown syntax shouting in your face for the whole draft.

builderNote: Replaced guessed tokens with iA's measured palettes (light #f9f9f9/#1c1c1c, dark #1a1a1a/#cccccc, caret #00b5ff on both, dim #cccccc/#707070, hairlines #e1e1e1/#313131, selection composited to iA's #003e4c) and kept the two grounds deliberately asymmetric rather than inverted. Added a --link token (accent blue is too pale for link text on paper), transparent chrome ground to match iA's panel-less toolbar, a quiet unfocused selection, a 160ms cross-fade armed only around a switch, live system-follow, prefers-contrast/print palettes, and iA's own appearance shortcut (Ctrl-Cmd-N / Ctrl+Alt+N). Verified no first-paint flash and correct ground for every stored/OS combination.
secondary: Neither shows any chrome — no counter, no bar, no scroll indicator, in either theme — so 'how the chrome sits on each ground' is untestable from these two frames.
Both use the identical accent #00b5ff for the caret in light and dark with no per-theme adjustment; on #f9f9f9 it is the highest-chroma element on the page.
Caret geometry: A 8x94 px with hard edges, B 9x94 px with antialiased sides — a wash.
Dark ink is 10.4:1 on both, against 15.2:1 in light: both dark themes are a third flatter than their light counterparts, neither compensates.
Line pitch is effectively identical (A ~94-96 px, B ~92-96 px); B's measure runs ~35 px narrower on the same viewport.
